stem: A solution contains $0.010$ M $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ and $0.020$ M $\text{Sr}^{2+}$. As $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ is added slowly, what is $[\text{Ba}^{2+}]$ when $\text{SrSO}_4$ just begins to precipitate? $K_{sp}(\text{BaSO}_4)=1.0\times10^{-10}$ and $K_{sp}(\text{SrSO}_4)=4.0\times10^{-7}$.

verdicts.working: SrSO₄ just begins to precipitate at [SO₄²⁻] = (4.0×10⁻⁷)/(0.020) = 2.0×10⁻⁵ M. BaSO₄ has already precipitated, so [Ba²⁺] = (1.0×10⁻¹⁰)/(2.0×10⁻⁵) = 5.0×10⁻⁶ M.

working:
$[\text{SO}_4^{2-}]_{\text{onset, Sr}}=\dfrac{K_{sp}(\text{SrSO}_4)}{[\text{Sr}^{2+}]}=\dfrac{4.0\times10^{-7}}{0.020}=2.0\times10^{-5}$ M
$[\text{Ba}^{2+}]=\dfrac{K_{sp}(\text{BaSO}_4)}{[\text{SO}_4^{2-}]}=\dfrac{1.0\times10^{-10}}{2.0\times10^{-5}}=5.0\times10^{-6}$ M

Independent check: SrSO₄ just begins to precipitate at [SO₄²⁻] = (4.0×10⁻⁷)/(0.020) = 2.0×10⁻⁵ M. BaSO₄ has already precipitated, so [Ba²⁺] = (1.0×10⁻¹⁰)/(2.0×10⁻⁵) = 5.0×10⁻⁶ M.
solution:
At the onset of SrSO₄ precipitation, $[\text{SO}_4^{2-}]=K_{sp}(\text{SrSO}_4)/[\text{Sr}^{2+}]=4.0\times10^{-7}/0.020=2.0\times10^{-5}\,\text{M}$.
BaSO₄ has already precipitated, so $[\text{Ba}^{2+}]=K_{sp}(\text{BaSO}_4)/[\text{SO}_4^{2-}]=1.0\times10^{-10}/(2.0\times10^{-5})=5.0\times10^{-6}\,\text{M}$.
